aline: Heads-up — ran a full seqlen-bucket sweep on GQA/MQA with paged-KV block sizes. Saw a weird regression in our autotuner's pick for 512-1024 seqlen range. attaching perf snippets in thread.

mike: can you paste the bench command?

aline: `./bench/run.sh --model llama-13b-gqa --mode pagedkv --bsize-sweep 32,64,128,256 --seq-buckets 64,128,256,512,1024 --runs 5`

sanjay: did the autotuner choose a different kernel than previous baseline?

aline: yes — for 512 seqlen it switched from kernel_v2_paged_attn (striped-block 128) -> kernel_v3_prefetch (interleaved bsize 64). throughput dropped ~12% and lat tail +40ms.

eva: that sounds like hysteresis in the hysteresis :) any recent commits around kernel scoring?

aline: commit 7c9d4f3 changed the scoring weights (lat_weight +0.1, mem_frag_penalty -0.2). suspect the lower frag penalty is favoring smaller blocks for MQA lanes.

dave: can you paste the small flame/summary?

aline: ```
# perf summary (512 seqlen, p99, tokens/s)
baseline kernel_v2_paged_attn (bsize128): 9.8k t/s, p99 210ms
autotune pick kernel_v3_prefetch (bsize64): 8.6k t/s, p99 250ms
memory util dropped 6% on-device, but more stalls due to extra prefetch work
```

ci-bot: Build 3128 deployed to canary (7c9d4f3). Perf regression alert triggered: +12% throughput drop for seqlen bucket 512.

mike: did you repro with deterministic pins (no background noise)?

aline: yes, repeated on two nodes, pinned to the same CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, cold start and warmed KV cache. regression still present.

sanjay: hypothesis: prefetch path increases instruction count and causes SM divergence on GQA multi-query lanes when blocksize crosses warp alignment. Also MQA per-head packing may misalign KV tile reuse.

eva: can we run microprofile comparing instruction count / occupancy between kernels?

dave: I'll trigger microprof on the same job. sharing command: `nvprof --metrics inst_executed,sm_efficiency,achieved_occupancy -- ./infer_bench --seq 512 --batch 1`

ci-bot: Microprofile job 457 queued.

mike: until we triage, can we pin autotuner to prefer blocksize>=128 for seqlen>=512? quick config override to avoid customer impact.

aline: good call. adding a temp heuristic: if seqlen >= 512 and model.arch == gqa then add +0.2 to bsize128 score. will push a canary config.

sanjay: long term we should add an instruction-count penalty into the kernel scorer so prefetch-heavy kernels don't win despite lower mem use.

eva: agree. also add a run that sweeps MQA lane counts (4,8,16) — pack factors matter.

dave: microprof results in: kernel_v3_prefetch shows inst_executed +18%, achieved_occupancy -7%, SM efficiency -9% vs kernel_v2. aligns with hypothesis.

aline: thanks dave. I'll revert the scoring commit and flip the canary config to prefer bsize128 for 512. planning to monitor 24h.

mike: postmortem-ish notes: 1) scoring change was too aggressive on frag penalty 2) need an instruction metric in autotuner 3) add seqlen hysteresis to avoid flip-flop on narrow deltas.

eva: also add autotune test in CI that asserts no >8% regression in any seqlen bucket relative to pinned baseline.

aline: will create the PR with revert + canary tweak + CI check. linking bench logs here: https://internal.redwood/bench/2418591222/logs

sanjay: thanks — once PR is up I'll run extended sweeps overnight across 128-2048 seqlens.

mike: :thumbsup: keep thread updated when CI finishes and canary perf stabilizes.
